data.name: Kitab
data.gender_notes: Kitab is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A reference to the Quran, the holy book of Islam. The name Kitab carries the meaning “The Book” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kitab usually hope their child will grow to embody the book and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of knowledge and guidance.
data.etymology: Kitab belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Book.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kitab total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: كتاب
in_arabic.long_meaning: كتاب هو كتاب الله تعالى، القرآن الكريم الذي أنزل على النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويعني أيضًا الكتاب المقدس أو الكتاب الذي يكتب فيه شيء ما، ويشير إلى القرآن كتاب الله الوحيد الذي لا شك فيه، وهو المصدر الرئيسي للتشريع الإسلامي

in_urdu.name: کتاب
in_urdu.long_meaning: کتاب کا مطلب ہے اللہ تعالیٰ کی کتاب، قرآن مجید جو حضرت محمد صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم پر نازل ہوا، اس کا مطلب کتاب مقدس یا کوئی بھی لکھی ہوئی چیز بھی ہو سکتا ہے، قرآن مجید اسلامی قانون کا بنیادی ذریعہ ہے اور مسلمانوں کے لئے مقدس کتاب ہے

in_hindi.name: किताब
in_hindi.long_meaning: किताब का अर्थ है अल्लाह की पुस्तक, कुरआन मजीद जो नबी मुहम्मद सल्लल्लाहु अलैहि वसल्लम पर उतारा गया, इसका अर्थ पवित्र पुस्तक या कोई भी लिखित बयान भी हो सकता है, कुरआन मजीद इस्लामी विधान का मुख्य स्रोत है और मुसलमानों के लिए पवित्र पुस्तक है

in_english.name: Kitab
in_english.meaning: The Book, Quran, Scripture, Written Record
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kitab originates from Arabic, referring to 'the book' or 'scripture'. It primarily denotes the Quran, the holy book of Islam revealed to Prophet Muhammad. The term encompasses the idea of a written record or divine scripture, serving as a central religious text in Islam. Etymologically, it relates to the Arabic root 'k-t-b', which conveys meanings related to writing and recording. Historically, Kitab holds immense spiritual significance as it represents the literal word of God as Muslims believe. In contemporary usage, Kitab symbolizes knowledge, guidance, and divine wisdom.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kitab" in Islamic culture carries a profound significance as it is synonymous with knowledge, wisdom, and guidance. In the Arabic language, the term means "book," but in the Islamic context, it is symbolic of the Quran, which Muslims believe to be the Word of Allah revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for the guidance of mankind. The Quran is not just a book but a source of laws, wisdom, and moral values that provide direction and meaning to the lives of Muslims.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, "Kitab" represents the binding force that connects Muslims to their Creator through the revelation of the Quran. Muslims revere the Quran as the ultimate truth and the divine guidance for all aspects of their lives. Reading and reciting the Quran is considered a religious practice that fosters a deep connection with Allah, leading to spiritual growth and enlightenment. To Muslims, the term "Kitab" is not just a name but a symbol of faith, hope, and wisdom, and the source of spiritual nourishment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "The Book" symbolizes A reference to the Quran, the holy book of Islam.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Kitab serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of the book.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The Kitab al-Fihrist is a 10th-century Arabic bibliography compiled by Ibn Al-Nadim. The name Kitab carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Al-Nadim's work is considered the oldest surviving book catalog in Arabic.

trends: used as a title for various works in Islamic studies
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Kitab remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Layla Kitab in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Kitab, which means "The Book". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.
